name: Charles Randolph
residence: Near Wheatland, Platte County (1 Richeau Road, south of Wheatland, per his 2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
occupation: Retired railroad dispatcher; he wrote that he had just short of 40 years of railroad experience, including 37 years as a dispatcher (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
education: Cheyenne Central High School, 1974; attended the University of Wyoming from 1974 off and on until 1976, majoring in astrophysics and computer science (2024 WyoFile questionnaire)
background: In his 2024 WyoFile questionnaire, Charles Randolph wrote that he and his wife, Susan, had lived since 2016 in a home south of Wheatland, just off Interstate 25 at the Slater exit. He wrote that he was born in Cheyenne in 1956, graduated from Central High School in 1974, lived in Wyoming until 1979, when work took him to McCook, Nebraska, and later Fort Worth, Texas, and that they returned to Wyoming when they retired in 2013. He said he would be 68 on Election Day 2024.

He wrote that he had just short of 40 years of railroad experience, including 37 years as a railroad dispatcher, 22 of them dispatching train movements along the Front Range and through Cheyenne, Chugwater, Wheatland, and from Orin Junction to Casper. He also wrote that he attended the University of Wyoming from 1974 off and on until 1976, majoring in astrophysics and computer science, and that as a student at McCormick Junior High and Cheyenne Central he sometimes sat in the House chambers after school while his mother, Shirley Randolph, worked at the Department of Education. He said he had served as a committeeman, precinct worker, and union representative, and had testified for stronger railroad safety rules.
